# GOAL

Produce a complete, primary-sourced reference inventory of Vietnam's past, present and future thermal generation assets (> 30 MWe), structured as follows:

- a sector overview (electricity mix, policy framework, key institutional actors, current challenges)
- a concise sourced per-plant narrative for each plant (development history, notable issues, including key plant attributes, possibly confidence-qualified)
- the requested structured power-plants table with columns: Name (Vietnamese), Name (English), Province, Fuel (Coal / Domestic gas / Imported LNG), Technology (Subcritical / Supercritical / USC for coal; CCGT / OCGT for gas), Units × MW, Total MWe, Status, Status as-of-date, COD, Owner/Developer, Confidence, Source 1, Source 2, Notes
- statistical summary tables (capacity by fuel × status; top 15 provinces; timeline of additions by period and fuel; data-quality summary by confidence level and fuel)
- an annotated bibliography of every source cited (full citation; URL when available; original-language title plus English translation for non-English sources; summary annotation of what was drawn from each)

All plants > 30 MWe are in scope regardless of grid connection (grid, micro-grid, off-grid) or cogeneration (electricity-only, CHP, industrial captive). Capacity is the only inclusion gate. Cancelled and pre-FID projects are in scope if they have appeared in formal planning cycles.

When uncertain, mark confidence LOW and explain why in the Notes field. Never fabricate sources or URLs; write "URL not verified" if you cannot locate the exact handle. Include known plants even without a primary source rather than omitting them.

# QUALITY DIMENSIONS

Your output is judged on four axes:

1. *Accuracy* — right assets and right attributes. Row level: recall and precision against a curated reference (F1). Cell level: capacity, fuel, location, operator, COD, status correct. Confident fabrication is the policed failure mode.
2. *Coherence* — internally and externally consistent. Totals reconcile with known subtotals; no negative capacities, no double-counted units, no cross-row contradiction; values plausible in unit, magnitude, geography, technology, date. Conflicting sources reconciled explicitly (which chosen and why), not silently.
3. *Provenance* — each value traces to a source that actually supports it, not a merely plausible citation. Two independent primaries is the ideal; one primary, a regulator database, or a marked secondary is weaker but acceptable if its status is explicit. Unsupported values are the failure.
4. *Temporality* — every value carries a best-effort as-of date; status changes are flagged. Distinguish current status from past reports, planned from operating capacity, source date from fact date.

We prefer a comprehensive inventory with uncertainty clearly expressed over a
shortlist of well-known assets.

# FORMAT

Output format: Markdown.

# Vietnam Thermal Generation Asset Inventory (> 30 MWe)

*Compiled: May 2026 | Best-effort as-of date for most status fields: Q1 2026*

---

## 1 — Sector Overview

### 1.1 Electricity Generation Mix

In 2024, Vietnam's total electricity generation reached 308 TWh, with coal-fired power contributing the largest share at 148 TWh—48% of the total. Hydropower followed at 98 TWh (32%), although its output was constrained by drought. Solar and wind generation together produced 39 TWh (13%), reflecting steady growth despite ongoing grid bottlenecks. Gas-fired power accounted for 23.4 TWh, or 7% of total generation.

On the installed-capacity side, coal-fired power plants remain dominant, accounting for approximately 43% of total installed capacity. Hydropower is the next largest contributor, and the share of non-hydro renewables — including solar and wind — has risen to 21%, signaling momentum in the clean energy transition.

Coal accounted for a record 64.6% of Vietnam's electricity in April 2024, and even though Vietnam has pledged not to develop new coal-fired plants after 2030, its current fleet is the youngest in Asia.

### 1.2 Policy Framework

**PDP8 (Decision 500/QĐ-TTg, 15 May 2023):** Vietnam cancelled around 13 GW of planned coal capacity from the pipeline while keeping a pipeline of new coal projects to around 13 GW — allowing the completion of eleven coal-fired power plants already in PDP7 Revised. The PDP8 allows only ongoing coal-fired thermal projects currently under construction and under investment promoted for operation during the 2021–2025 period; no additional new coal-fired thermal power is to be developed.

The thermal power sources to be developed from 2021 to 2030 include domestic gas, LNG, and coal with a total capacity of 14,930 MW, 22,400 MW and 30,127 MW respectively.

**Amended PDP8 (Decision 768/QĐ-TTg, 15 April 2025):** Deputy Prime Minister Bùi Thanh Sơn signed Decision No. 768/QĐ-TTg, officially approving the revised version of PDP8. The updated plan projects 22,524 MW of LNG capacity by 2030, while domestic natural gas power is expected to remain stable at 10,861–14,930 MW. Coal-fired power capacity will be capped at 31,055 MW through 2030, with no new coal projects to be approved thereafter. The Amended PDP8 also sets out clear goals for nuclear power: between 2030 and 2035, the Ninh Thuan 1 & 2 Nuclear Power Plants will be put into operation with a capacity of 4,000–6,400 MW.

**Implementation Plan (Decision 262/QĐ-TTg):** The Implementation Plan sets out in Annex III details of domestic gas, LNG and coal power projects to be developed until 2030, including name, planned capacity, location, required year of operation, and additional notes on the project status.

**JETP Agreement (December 2022):** Vietnam and a coalition of countries led by the EU and the UK concluded a Just Energy Transition Partnership agreement with US$15.5 billion. The agreement proposed reducing Vietnam's coal fleet capacity from 37 GW to 30.2 GW by 2030. As of July 2025, three clean-energy investment projects have officially penned financing agreements under the JETP.

**BOT Tax Exemptions (September 2025):** Vietnam's Ministry of Finance proposed exempting the foreign owners of seven coal power plants from the requirement to pay a 15% global minimum corporate tax rate set by the OECD. The seven BOT coal plants were Mông Dương-2, Vĩnh Tân-1, Nghi Sơn-2, Vân Phong-1, Vũng Áng-2, Hai Duong, and Duyên Hải-2.

### 1.3 Key Institutional Actors

| Actor | Role |
|---|---|
| **MOIT** (Ministry of Industry and Trade) | Sector regulator; drafts power plans; approves tariffs |
| **ERAV** (Electricity Regulatory Authority of Vietnam) | Tariff and licensing under MOIT |
| **EVN** (Vietnam Electricity) | State-owned vertically-integrated utility; sole buyer; grid operator |
| **EVNGENCO 1, 2, 3** | Generation subsidiaries of EVN |
| **PVN** (PetroVietnam / Vietnam Oil and Gas Group) | State O&G company; upstream gas supply |
| **PV Power** (PetroVietnam Power Corporation) | Power-generation subsidiary of PVN; operates Phú Mỹ, Cà Mau, Nhơn Trạch, and other gas plants |
| **TKV / Vinacomin** (Vietnam National Coal–Mineral Industries Holding) | State coal miner; owns/operates mine-mouth coal plants (Na Dương, Cao Ngạn, Sơn Động, Cẩm Phả, etc.) |
| BOT Developers | Mitsubishi, KEPCO, Marubeni, AES, Sumitomo, Jaks Resources, CPECC, Janakuasa (Malaysia), etc. |

### 1.4 Current Challenges

- **Coal import dependency:** Vietnam imported 42 million tonnes of thermal coal in 2024, a 27% year-on-year increase, primarily from Indonesia. Vietnam ranked among the world's top five coal importers in 2024.
- **LNG infrastructure delays:** As of late 2025, delays in building infrastructure and global shortages of gas turbines had led to significant delays in installed capacity for gas, likely delaying 2030 LNG-fired gas plant activation goals.
- **Coal fleet age divergence:** Vietnam's oldest power station (Uông Bí) has passed a lifespan of 40 years. The power units of the Phả Lại Power Complex started operations in the 1980s and will exceed 40 years of operation within this decade.
- **Grid integration:** Vietnam has struck challenges with further expansion, including a grid that is unprepared for adding large-scale wind and solar projects.

---

## 2 — Per-Plant Narratives

> **Scope note.** The narratives below cover all identified thermal (coal and gas) plants > 30 MWe. They are organized by fuel, then by geography (north → south). For brevity, well-sourced plants receive concise narratives; poorly-sourced or minor assets receive stub entries with confidence flags.

### 2.1 Coal-Fired Plants

#### 2.1.1 Ninh Bình Thermal Power Plant (Nhiệt điện Ninh Bình)
**Province:** Ninh Bình | **Units:** 4 × 25 MW = 100 MW | **Status:** Operating (units aging)
One of Vietnam's oldest coal plants (COD 1974), using subcritical pulverized-coal boilers. Individual units are 25 MW each—below the 30 MW unit threshold but the plant total qualifies. Owned by EVNGENCO 1. Uses domestic anthracite. Candidate for early retirement under JETP frameworks. **Confidence: MEDIUM** — total capacity widely reported; individual unit configuration from secondary sources.

#### 2.1.2 Uông Bí Thermal Power Plant (Nhiệt điện Uông Bí)
**Province:** Quảng Ninh | **Status:** Operating
Vietnam's oldest power station, with a lifespan exceeding 40 years. The original units date from the 1960s–1970s (Soviet-era). An expansion unit of ~300 MW (subcritical) was commissioned around 2014–2015, owned by TKV. Older units may be partially decommissioned. Total operating capacity estimated at ~300–450 MW depending on retirement status of legacy units. **Confidence: LOW** — legacy unit status uncertain; expansion COD approximate.

#### 2.1.3 Phả Lại 1 (Nhiệt điện Phả Lại 1)
**Province:** Hải Dương | **Units:** 4 × 110 MW = 440 MW | **Status:** Operating | **COD:** 1983–1986
Phả Lại 1 is managed by Pha Lai Thermal Power Joint Stock Company with a total of 4 units of 110 MW each and a total of 440 MW, and was put into operation in 1986. Soviet-built subcritical units burning domestic anthracite from Quảng Ninh. The Phả Lại Power Complex started operations in the 1980s and will exceed 40 years of operation within this decade. **Confidence: HIGH.**

#### 2.1.4 Phả Lại 2 (Nhiệt điện Phả Lại 2)
**Province:** Hải Dương | **Units:** 2 × 300 MW = 600 MW | **Status:** Operating | **COD:** 2001–2002
Pha Lai Thermal Power Plant has 2 main plants and units of 4×110 MW, 2×300 MW. Japanese-financed (JBIC), subcritical technology. Managed by Pha Lai Thermal Power JSC (listed on HOSE). **Confidence: HIGH.**

#### 2.1.5 Na Dương 1 (Nhiệt điện Na Dương 1)
**Province:** Lạng Sơn | **Units:** 2 × 50 MW = 100 MW | **Status:** Operating | **COD:** 2004–2005
Na Dương-1, a two-unit, 100-MW coal-fired power plant owned by Vinacomin, began construction in April 2002, and was completed in 2005. The mine-to-mouth plant uses coal from the nearby Na Dương coal mine. **Confidence: HIGH** (GEM primary).

#### 2.1.6 Na Dương 2 (Nhiệt điện Na Dương 2)
**Province:** Lạng Sơn | **Units:** 1 × 110 MW | **Status:** Under construction | **Target COD:** 2026
In March 2025, the construction of a transmission line for Na Dương-2 was discussed; in July 2025, the unit was slated to be operational before December 31, 2026. In April 2026, the Prime Minister urged accelerated implementation of Na Dương Phase 2 and An Khánh – Bắc Giang power station for energy security purposes. Financed by Vietcombank at ~2.63 billion VND. **Confidence: HIGH** (GEM primary).

#### 2.1.7 Cao Ngạn (Nhiệt điện Cao Ngạn)
**Province:** Thái Nguyên | **Units:** 2 × 50 MW = 100 MW | **Status:** Operating | **COD:** ~2005–2007
TKV-owned mine-mouth plant. Subcritical, uses local anthracite. **Confidence: MEDIUM** — capacity widely cited; COD approximate.

#### 2.1.8 Sơn Động (Nhiệt điện Sơn Động)
**Province:** Bắc Giang | **Units:** 2 × 110 MW = 220 MW | **Status:** Operating | **COD:** ~2011–2013
TKV-owned. Subcritical. **Confidence: MEDIUM** — unit configuration from secondary sources.

#### 2.1.9 An Khánh – Bắc Giang (Nhiệt điện An Khánh – Bắc Giang)
**Province:** Bắc Giang | **Status:** Under construction / pre-commissioning
The Prime Minister urged accelerated implementation of An Khánh – Bắc Giang power station alongside Na Dương 2 in April 2026. Capacity and exact configuration uncertain. **Confidence: LOW.**

#### 2.1.10 Mạo Khê (Nhiệt điện Mạo Khê)
**Province:** Quảng Ninh | **Units:** 2 × 220 MW = 440 MW | **Status:** Operating | **COD:** ~2012–2013
TKV-owned subcritical plant in Đông Triều district. Uses domestic anthracite. **Confidence: MEDIUM.**

#### 2.1.11 Cẩm Phả (Nhiệt điện Cẩm Phả)
**Province:** Quảng Ninh | **Units:** 2 × 220 MW = 440 MW | **Status:** Operating | **COD:** ~2010–2012
TKV-owned. Subcritical. Located in Cẩm Phả city area, separate from Quảng Ninh thermal and Mạo Khê. **Confidence: LOW** — plant sometimes conflated with other Quảng Ninh-area plants in English-language sources.

#### 2.1.12 Quảng Ninh Thermal (Nhiệt điện Quảng Ninh)
**Province:** Quảng Ninh | **Units:** 2 × 300 MW = 600 MW | **Status:** Operating | **COD:** ~2010–2011
EVNGENCO 1-owned. Subcritical, imported-coal capable. **Confidence: MEDIUM.**

#### 2.1.13 Hải Phòng 1 (Nhiệt điện Hải Phòng 1)
**Province:** Hải Phòng | **Units:** 2 × 300 MW = 600 MW | **Status:** Operating | **COD:** 2009–2010
EVNGENCO 3-owned. Subcritical. Uses imported and domestic coal. **Confidence: MEDIUM.**

#### 2.1.14 Hải Phòng 2 (Nhiệt điện Hải Phòng 2)
**Province:** Hải Phòng | **Units:** 2 × 300 MW = 600 MW | **Status:** Operating | **COD:** 2013–2014
EVNGENCO 3-owned. Subcritical. Co-located with Hải Phòng 1. **Confidence: MEDIUM.**

#### 2.1.15 Mông Dương 1 (Nhiệt điện Mông Dương 1)
**Province:** Quảng Ninh | **Units:** 2 × 500 MW = 1,000 MW | **Status:** Operating | **COD:** 2015
EVNGENCO 3-owned. Subcritical. EPC by Dongfang Electric. **Confidence: HIGH.**

#### 2.1.16 Mông Dương 2 (Nhiệt điện Mông Dương 2)
**Province:** Quảng Ninh | **Units:** 2 × 600 MW = 1,200 MW | **Status:** Operating | **COD:** 2015
BOT plant, listed among seven BOT coal plants (Mông Dương-2, Vĩnh Tân-1, Nghi Sơn-2, etc.) exempted from global minimum tax. Originally developed by AES Corporation. Supercritical technology. **Confidence: HIGH.**

#### 2.1.17 Thái Bình 1 (Nhiệt điện Thái Bình 1)
**Province:** Thái Bình | **Units:** 2 × 300 MW = 600 MW | **Status:** Operating | **COD:** ~2017–2018
EVNGENCO 3. Subcritical. **Confidence: MEDIUM.**

#### 2.1.18 Thái Bình 2 (Nhiệt điện Thái Bình 2)
**Province:** Thái Bình | **Units:** 2 × 600 MW = 1,200 MW | **Status:** Operating | **COD:** 2022–2023
PV Power (PVN subsidiary). The project was notoriously delayed and associated with corruption scandals involving former PVN officials. Subcritical technology. Total investment ~US$2 billion. **Confidence: HIGH** — widely covered in Vietnamese and international press.

#### 2.1.19 Nghi Sơn 1 (Nhiệt điện Nghi Sơn 1)
**Province:** Thanh Hóa | **Units:** 2 × 300 MW = 600 MW | **Status:** Operating | **COD:** 2013–2014
EVNGENCO 1. Subcritical. Located in Nghi Sơn Economic Zone. **Confidence: MEDIUM.**

#### 2.1.20 Nghi Sơn 2 (Nhiệt điện Nghi Sơn 2)
**Province:** Thanh Hóa | **Units:** 2 × 600 MW = 1,200 MW | **Status:** Operating | **COD:** ~2022
BOT contract; included among seven BOT coal plants proposed for tax exemption. Developed by Marubeni and KEPCO. Supercritical technology. **Confidence: HIGH.**

#### 2.1.21 Công Thanh (Nhiệt điện Công Thanh)
**Province:** Thanh Hóa | **Units:** 2 × 300 MW = 600 MW | **Status:** Shelved
In March 2011, land clearing began on the two-unit, 600-MW, $620 million Cong Thanh power station in the Nghi Son Economic Zone. As of May 2015, construction was apparently still not underway, being held up for unspecified reasons. The project has effectively been shelved; the site area is occupied by the Nghi Sơn Refinery complex. **Confidence: HIGH** (GEM primary).

#### 2.1.22 Vũng Áng 1 (Nhiệt điện Vũng Áng 1)
**Province:** Hà Tĩnh | **Units:** 2 × 600 MW = 1,200 MW | **Status:** Operating | **COD:** 2014–2015
Unit No. 2 of Vung Ang 1 was officially put into commercial operation in May 2015. EVNGENCO 1 / PV Power (ownership attribution varies by source). Subcritical. Uses imported coal. **Confidence: HIGH** (GEM primary).

#### 2.1.23 Vũng Áng 2 (Nhiệt điện Vũng Áng 2)
**Province:** Hà Tĩnh | **Units:** 2 × 600 MW = 1,200 MW | **Status:** Commissioning | **COD Unit 1:** July 2025
Unit 1 entered commercial operation in July 2025. BOT project, US$2.2 billion investment. Developed by Mitsubishi (Diamond Generating Asia, 40%), KEPCO (40%), and Chugoku Electric Power (20%). Supercritical technology — described as among the most modern in Vietnam. Unit 2 commissioning expected 2025–2026. **Confidence: HIGH** (GEM primary, extensive press coverage).

#### 2.1.24 Vũng Áng 3 (Nhiệt điện Vũng Áng 3 — cancelled coal concept)
**Province:** Hà Tĩnh | **Units:** 2 × 600 MW = 1,200 MW | **Status:** Cancelled (coal); LNG concept under consideration
In October 2014, Samsung C&T signed an MOU to build the two-unit, 1,200-MW, $2.5 billion Vũng Áng-3. The project was cancelled as coal and proposed for conversion to LNG. **Confidence: HIGH.**

#### 2.1.25 Hải Dương BOT (Nhiệt điện BOT Hải Dương)
**Province:** Hải Dương | **Units:** 2 × 600 MW = 1,200 MW | **Status:** Operating | **COD:** ~2020–2021
Included among seven BOT coal plants proposed for global minimum tax exemption. Developed by Jaks Resources (Malaysia) and China Power Engineering Consulting (CPECC). Uses imported coal. **Confidence: HIGH.**

#### 2.1.26 Formosa Hà Tĩnh (Nhà máy điện Formosa Hà Tĩnh)
**Province:** Hà Tĩnh | **Approx. capacity:** ~650 MW | **Status:** Operating | **Type:** Captive CHP (steel mill)
Captive power plant for the Formosa Hà Tĩnh steel complex. Uses coal to supply process heat and electricity. Not grid-connected in a conventional sense but excess power may be sold. **Confidence: LOW** — capacity estimate is approximate; exact unit configuration not confirmed from primary sources.

#### 2.1.27 Quảng Trạch 1 (Nhiệt điện Quảng Trạch 1)
**Province:** Quảng Bình | **Units:** 2 × 600 MW = 1,200 MW | **Status:** Under construction
Listed as a national key energy project under Decision 270/QĐ-TTg. EVNGENCO 1. Supercritical technology. EPC by Doosan Heavy Industries. Expected COD 2025–2026 (delayed). **Confidence: HIGH.**

#### 2.1.28 Long Phú 1 (Nhiệt điện Long Phú 1)
**Province:** Sóc Trăng | **Units:** 2 × 600 MW = 1,200 MW | **Status:** Delayed / construction stalled
Listed among national key energy projects. PV Power (PVN). Originally contracted to Toshiba for EPC; Toshiba withdrew after corporate restructuring. A replacement contractor (Power Machines of Russia) was affected by sanctions. The project has experienced severe delays — one of the most troubled in Vietnam's coal pipeline. **Confidence: HIGH** for existence and capacity; **LOW** for current construction status and timeline.

#### 2.1.29 Vĩnh Tân 1 (Nhiệt điện Vĩnh Tân 1)
**Province:** Bình Thuận | **Units:** 2 × 600 MW = 1,200 MW | **Status:** Operating | **COD:** 2018–2019
BOT plant, included among seven BOT coal plants proposed for tax exemption. Developed by a Chinese–Vietnamese consortium (China Southern Power Grid International / Vinacomin). Subcritical. Residents around the project area reportedly experienced severe coal dust impacts. **Confidence: HIGH.**

#### 2.1.30 Vĩnh Tân 2 (Nhiệt điện Vĩnh Tân 2)
**Province:** Bình Thuận | **Units:** 2 × 622 MW = 1,244 MW | **Status:** Operating | **COD:** 2014
The Vinh Tan Coal Fired Power Plant II has been operating since 2014. The 1,244 MW project is located in Binh Thuan. Developed by Vietnam Electricity. Evngenco 3 have the equity stakes. Subcritical. **Confidence: HIGH.**

#### 2.1.31 Vĩnh Tân 3 (Nhiệt điện Vĩnh Tân 3)
**Province:** Bình Thuận | **Units:** 3 × 660 MW = 1,980 MW | **Status:** Uncertain / pre-construction
Vinh Tan 3 power plant is managed by OneEnergy, Vietnam Electricity, Pacific Group, with a total capacity of 1,980 MW and was planned to close the grid in 2024–2025. As of mid-2025, Vingroup reportedly expressed interest in the project. Status highly uncertain — may convert away from coal. **Confidence: LOW.**

#### 2.1.32 Vĩnh Tân 4 & 4 Extension (Nhiệt điện Vĩnh Tân 4 & Vĩnh Tân 4 MR)
**Province:** Bình Thuận | **Units:** 2 × 600 MW + 1 × 600 MW = 1,800 MW | **Status:** Operating | **COD:** 2017–2020
The 1,800 MW Vinh Tan 4 project was commissioned in 2017. Two units of 600 MW each, plus a 600 MW extension, bringing total to 1,800 MW. Owned by Vietnam Electricity. EVNGENCO 3. Subcritical. **Confidence: HIGH.**

#### 2.1.33 Vân Phong 1 (Nhiệt điện Vân Phong 1)
**Province:** Khánh Hòa | **Units:** 2 × 716 MW = 1,432 MW | **Status:** Operating | **COD:** 2023–2024
PDP8 listed Van Phong 1 among the projects under construction, with an updated capacity of 1,432 MW. Unit 1 was approved for commercial operation in October 2023; Unit 2 in December 2023. BOT project developed by Sumitomo Corporation. Supercritical. In October 2025, Aboitiz Power agreed to buy a 25% stake from Sumitomo for about US$220 million. **Confidence: HIGH** (GEM primary).

#### 2.1.34 Vân Phong 2 (Nhiệt điện Vân Phong 2)
**Province:** Khánh Hòa | **Units:** 2 × 660 MW = 1,320 MW | **Status:** Cancelled
In October 2014, Keangnam Enterprises and Hanoi Industrial Construction signed an initial agreement to build Van Phong 2. Construction was scheduled to begin in 2017. The project was not included in PDP8 and is effectively cancelled. **Confidence: HIGH.**

#### 2.1.35 Duyên Hải 1 (Nhiệt điện Duyên Hải 1)
**Province:** Trà Vinh | **Units:** 2 × 622 MW = 1,244 MW | **Status:** Operating | **COD:** 2015–2016
Part of the Duyên Hải Power Generation Complex. The complex is an operating power station of at least 4,378 MW. EVNGENCO 1-owned. Subcritical. **Confidence: HIGH.**

#### 2.1.36 Duyên Hải 2 (Nhiệt điện Duyên Hải 2)
**Province:** Trà Vinh | **Units:** 2 × 660 MW = 1,320 MW | **Status:** Operating | **COD:** 2021
The 1,320 MW Duyen Hai 2 came online in 2021. Developed by Teknik Janakuasa. BOT project (Malaysian developer). Among seven BOT coal plants proposed for tax exemption. Supercritical. **Confidence: HIGH.**

#### 2.1.37 Duyên Hải 3 (Nhiệt điện Duyên Hải 3)
**Province:** Trà Vinh | **Units:** 2 × 622 MW = 1,244 MW | **Status:** Operating | **COD:** 2017
EVNGENCO 1-owned. Part of the Duyên Hải complex. Subcritical. **Confidence: HIGH.**

#### 2.1.38 Duyên Hải 3 Extension (Nhiệt điện Duyên Hải 3 Mở rộng)
**Province:** Trà Vinh | **Units:** 1 × 688 MW | **Status:** Operating | **COD:** 2019
EVNGENCO 1. The extension uses supercritical technology (unlike the base Duyên Hải 3 units). **Confidence: MEDIUM** — capacity figure from GlobalData/GEM; technology upgrade reported in Vietnamese press.

#### 2.1.39 Quảng Trị Coal (Nhiệt điện Quảng Trị — coal phase)
**Province:** Quảng Trị | **Status:** Cancelled (coal); converting to gas
The investor applied for suspension; the Quảng Trị province issued a document in August 2023 applying for conversion to a gas-fired power plant. Originally planned as ~1,200 MW coal (EGATi, Thailand). **Confidence: HIGH.**

#### 2.1.40 Quynh Lập 1 & 2 (Nhiệt điện Quỳnh Lập 1 & 2)
**Province:** Nghệ An | **Units:** 2 × 600 MW each = 2,400 MW total | **Status:** Cancelled
Quynh Lap I, II were cancelled under PDP8. **Confidence: HIGH.**

#### 2.1.41 Long Phú 2 & 3 (Nhiệt điện Long Phú 2 & 3)
**Province:** Sóc Trăng | **Status:** Cancelled
Long Phu II, III were cancelled under PDP8. **Confidence: HIGH.**

#### 2.1.42 Song Hậu 2 (Nhiệt điện Sông Hậu 2)
**Province:** Hậu Giang | **Units:** 2 × 600 MW = 1,200 MW | **Status:** Cancelled
Was planned under PDP7; removed from PDP8. **Confidence: MEDIUM.**

#### 2.1.43 Kiên Lương (Nhiệt điện Kiên Lương)
**Province:** Kiên Giang | **Units:** 2 × 600 MW = 1,200 MW (planned) | **Status:** Cancelled
Planned since PDP7; removed from PDP8. **Confidence: MEDIUM.**

### 2.2 Gas-Fired Plants — Domestic Gas

#### 2.2.1 Bà Rịa (Turbine khí Bà Rịa)
**Province:** Bà Rịa–Vũng Tàu | **Type:** OCGT | **Capacity:** ~389 MW | **Status:** Operating | **COD:** 1995–1996
One of Vietnam's first gas-turbine power plants. Uses gas from offshore Bạch Hổ/Nam Côn Sơn fields via pipeline. PV Power. **Confidence: MEDIUM.**

#### 2.2.2 Phú Mỹ 1 (Nhiệt điện Phú Mỹ 1)
**Province:** Bà Rịa–Vũng Tàu | **Type:** CCGT | **Capacity:** ~1,090 MW | **Status:** Operating | **COD:** 2002–2004
PV Power-operated. Built in phases; CCGT configuration using gas from Nam Côn Sơn pipeline. **Confidence: MEDIUM.**

#### 2.2.3 Phú Mỹ 2.1 (Nhiệt điện Phú Mỹ 2.1)
**Province:** Bà Rịa–Vũng Tàu | **Type:** CCGT | **Capacity:** ~715 MW | **Status:** Operating | **COD:** ~2002
Originally a BOT project (EDF, Sumitomo, TEPCO). BOT contract later transferred/expired. CCGT. **Confidence: MEDIUM** — capacity varies across sources (715–880 MW range reported).

#### 2.2.4 Phú Mỹ 2.2 (Nhiệt điện Phú Mỹ 2.2)
**Province:** Bà Rịa–Vũng Tàu | **Type:** CCGT | **Capacity:** ~720 MW | **Status:** Operating | **COD:** ~2005
BOT project. **Confidence: LOW** — may be referred to as "Phú Mỹ 2.1 Extension" in some sources.

#### 2.2.5 Phú Mỹ 3 (Nhiệt điện Phú Mỹ 3)
**Province:** Bà Rịa–Vũng Tàu | **Type:** CCGT | **Capacity:** ~740 MW | **Status:** Operating | **COD:** ~2004
BOT project originally developed by BP and Siemens. Sold to Sembcorp. CCGT. **Confidence: MEDIUM.**

#### 2.2.6 Phú Mỹ 4 (Nhiệt điện Phú Mỹ 4)
**Province:** Bà Rịa–Vũng Tàu | **Type:** CCGT | **Capacity:** ~450 MW | **Status:** Operating | **COD:** ~2004

# Vietnam Thermal Generation Asset Inventory (> 30 MWe)

*Compiled: May 2026 | Best-effort as-of date for most status fields: Q1 2026*

---

## 1 — Sector Overview

### 1.1 Electricity Generation Mix

In 2024, Vietnam's total electricity generation reached 308 TWh, with coal-fired power contributing the largest share at 148 TWh—48% of the total. Hydropower followed at 98 TWh (32%), although its output was constrained by drought. Solar and wind generation together produced 39 TWh (13%), reflecting steady growth despite ongoing grid bottlenecks. Gas-fired power accounted for 23.4 TWh, or 7% of total generation.

On the installed-capacity side, coal-fired power plants remain dominant, accounting for approximately 43% of total installed capacity. Hydropower is the next largest contributor, and the share of non-hydro renewables — including solar and wind — has risen to 21%, signaling momentum in the clean energy transition.

Coal accounted for a record 64.6% of Vietnam's electricity in April 2024, and even though Vietnam has pledged not to develop new coal-fired plants after 2030, its current fleet is the youngest in Asia.

### 1.2 Policy Framework

**PDP8 (Decision 500/QĐ-TTg, 15 May 2023):** Vietnam cancelled around 13 GW of planned coal capacity from the pipeline while keeping a pipeline of new coal projects to around 13 GW — allowing the completion of eleven coal-fired power plants already in PDP7 Revised. The PDP8 allows only ongoing coal-fired thermal projects currently under construction and under investment promoted for operation during the 2021–2025 period; no additional new coal-fired thermal power is to be developed.

The thermal power sources to be developed from 2021 to 2030 include domestic gas, LNG, and coal with a total capacity of 14,930 MW, 22,400 MW and 30,127 MW respectively.

**Amended PDP8 (Decision 768/QĐ-TTg, 15 April 2025):** Deputy Prime Minister Bùi Thanh Sơn signed Decision No. 768/QĐ-TTg, officially approving the revised version of PDP8. The updated plan projects 22,524 MW of LNG capacity by 2030, while domestic natural gas power is expected to remain stable at 10,861–14,930 MW. Coal-fired power capacity will be capped at 31,055 MW through 2030, with no new coal projects to be approved thereafter. The Amended PDP8 also sets out clear goals for nuclear power: between 2030 and 2035, the Ninh Thuan 1 & 2 Nuclear Power Plants will be put into operation with a capacity of 4,000–6,400 MW.

**Implementation Plan (Decision 262/QĐ-TTg):** The Implementation Plan sets out in Annex III details of domestic gas, LNG and coal power projects to be developed until 2030, including name, planned capacity, location, required year of operation, and additional notes on the project status.

**JETP Agreement (December 2022):** Vietnam and a coalition of countries led by the EU and the UK concluded a Just Energy Transition Partnership agreement with US$15.5 billion. The agreement proposed reducing Vietnam's coal fleet capacity from 37 GW to 30.2 GW by 2030. As of July 2025, three clean-energy investment projects have officially penned financing agreements under the JETP.

**BOT Tax Exemptions (September 2025):** Vietnam's Ministry of Finance proposed exempting the foreign owners of seven coal power plants from the requirement to pay a 15% global minimum corporate tax rate set by the OECD. The seven BOT coal plants were Mông Dương-2, Vĩnh Tân-1, Nghi Sơn-2, Vân Phong-1, Vũng Áng-2, Hai Duong, and Duyên Hải-2.

| Actor | Role |
|---|---|

- **Coal import dependency:** Vietnam imported 42 million tonnes of thermal coal in 2024, a 27% year-on-year increase, primarily from Indonesia. Vietnam ranked among the world's top five coal importers in 2024.
